Ag ~600 g/t all-grade assumed × 90%; incremental cost estimate. Standard smelter credit.

Tnuva (whey source) + NVIDIA (server-board ITAD) + Carasso: dairy side stream recovers gold from data-centre e-waste

Yield = 100 g/t × 90% (paper recovers ~90.8 wt% Au nuggets from motherboard leachate). Cost estimate excludes Cu pre-leach (in Cu route); whey protein aerogel ~1 kg per 6 kg Au, negligible per kg board. Strong hackathon demo: whey fibrillation 90 °C pH2 + freeze-dry + Au capture visible colour change.
pyrolysis 500-600 °C of glass-fibre/epoxy NMF with HBr capture in alkaline scrubber; NaBr returned to bromine producer
TBBPA-epoxy releases HBr during pyrolysis; scrubbing yields NaBr/HBr that can be oxidised to Br2 at a bromine plant, closing the BFR loop.
ICL (non-sponsor) bromine loop; Tosaf (BFR additive users)

Yield estimate: board Br ~4% (BFR boards typically 3-6% Br) × 70% capture, expressed as Br. Process cost left blank (no TEA found). Value small; pitch is closing ICL Br loop + clean glass fibre for reuse.

PCB non-metallic fraction (glass-fibre/epoxy) reinforcing filler for PP/PE compounds

Price estimate: set at ~40% of talc/glass-fibre filler cost (~$1/kg range) because BFR content limits applications. Yield = 70% NMF share × ~85% fine-grade recovery. Published in many Chinese studies (NMF-PP composites), some commercial in China, so novelty 3.

Raising pH >10.5 precipitates Mg2+ (~2.6 g/kg in 2× seawater) as brucite.

Yield = 2.6 g Mg/kg × (58.3/24.3) × 80%. Cost estimate: NaOH 0.21 mol/kg brine ≈8.6 g × $0.5/kg ≈ $0.004 + handling. Saudi SWA runs a Mg-from-brine plant (for remineralisation), so novelty 2. Sorek 2 (IDE, operating since Mar 2025) is greenfield-ish and already has on-site chemical production.

Cl2 oxidises Br- (~130 mg/kg) to Br2, which is stripped and condensed.
Yield = 130 mg/kg × 80% (Br estimate from stream record). Cost estimate ≈ value; at 130 mg/kg Br the blow-out process is marginal vs Dead Sea brines (~5 g/kg); included as baseline.

direct lithium extraction (Li-selective sorbent λ-MnO2/H2TiO3 or Li-selective membrane electrodialysis)

Yield expressed as Li2CO3: 0.35 mg Li/kg × 5.32 × 70% ≈ 1.3e-6 kg/kg → gross ~$0.00002/kg: uneconomic standalone; only viable piggy-backed on Mg/Br train. Cost blank (no TEA at 0.35 ppm).

Layered double hydroxide sorbent (from brine Mg + Al waste)
Layered double hydroxide sorbent (from brine Mg + Al waste)
co-precipitation pH 10 at Mg:Al 3:1 in CO2-sparged brine, ageing 60 °C, wash, dry
Brine Mg2+ and waste aluminate co-precipitate as Mg-Al layered double hydroxide (hydrotalcite) whose anion-exchange layers capture phosphate, arsenate, PFAS or boron.

Yield = 2.6 g Mg/kg × 4.1 kg LDH per kg Mg (Mg3Al(OH)8(CO3)0.5·2H2O) × 80%. Cost estimate (aluminate is a waste, NaOH balance, drying) ~$0.03/kg brine. LDH price $10/kg is speciality sorbent grade; market far smaller than brine volume.

Bipolar membranes split water at the junction so Na+ and Cl- leave as NaOH and HCl without chlorine gas.
Strauss/Tnuva/Magnum: locally produced NaOH for CIP; Sorek 2 on-site chemicals

Yield estimate: NaCl ~60 g/kg → max 41 g NaOH, 50% conversion. Cost estimate: BMED ~2-3 kWh/kg NaOH at $0.1/kWh ≈ $0.3/kg NaOH → $0.006 + NF pretreatment. Low-concentration product (~1-2 M) needs local use. Several EU pilots (e.g. SEArcularMINE/WATER-MINING) exist.

High pH brine absorbs CO2 as carbonate which precipitates with residual Ca2+/Mg2+, permanently mineralising CO2.

Yield estimate: residual Ca ~0.9 g/kg (2× seawater 0.41 g/kg) → CaCO3 2.2 g + some Mg carbonate ≈4 g/kg. CO2 stored ≈ 0.44×yield. Price of P0153 ($0.03) is mainly the carbon credit; value mostly in CO2 removal accounting. Sorek 2 already captures its CHP CO2 for remineralisation.

Yield = 0.85×(40/58.4)×90%. Cost estimate: ~2.4 MWh/t NaOH × $0.1/kWh ≈ $0.24/kg NaOH ×0.52 + purification. Value also in Cl2 (not counted). Chlor-alkali is mature; using Sdom salt waste with on-site Cl2 demand is the novel pairing.

electrochemical NaOH (or ammonia-Solvay) + carbonation with biogenic CO2 → NaHCO3 precipitation, calcine to Na2CO3

Price estimate: global soda ash ~$250-350/t (2024-25 market range). Yield = 0.85×(106/117)×75%. Israel imports all soda ash (glass, detergents, Na-ion battery precursors). CO2 avoided rough: ~0.4 kg CO2 bound per kg Na2CO3 minus energy.

The MgCl2 fraction plus MgO forms magnesium oxychloride (Sorel) cement that binds NaCl grains into hygroscopic-resistant blocks for arid-climate walls/sea-level barrier ("salt wall").

Yield = 50% solids × ~85% after calcination LOI. Price = LC3 cement value ($0.1) used conservatively. Suitability depends on clay kaolinite content (Israeli quarries are mostly carbonate). CO2 avoided vs OPC clinker substitution ~0.6 kg/kg SCM, halved for uncertainty.

Stored urine reaches pH 9 so PO4 + NH4 + added Mg precipitate as MgNH4PO4·6H2O.

Nitrifiers convert volatile ammonia to non-volatile ammonium nitrate so urine can be evaporated without N loss into a complete liquid fertiliser.
Commercial in Switzerland (Vuna "Aurin", authorised fertiliser). Price estimate per kg concentrate (~50 g N/kg + premium). Collection infrastructure (no-mix toilets) is the bottleneck in Israel.

microbially induced calcite precipitation: Sporosarcina pasteurii urease in sand moulds, 4-6 d curing
Urease hydrolyses urea to CO3^2- and NH4+; with brine Ca2+ calcite precipitates and cements sand grains at ambient temperature.

Concept demonstrated at Univ. of Cape Town (2018 urine bio-bricks). Yield estimate: brick mass attributable per kg urine (rough, depends on number of feed cycles). Dead Sea end brine as Ca source is the novel pairing.

photobioreactor cultivation of Chlorella/Scenedesmus on urine N/P/K
Urine supplies all macro-nutrients (N, P, K, S) for microalgae; biomass (non-food) used as biostimulant/biofertiliser.
Yield estimate: 8 g N/L ÷ ~8% N in algae × ~50% uptake. Price P0155 ($5) is feed-grade; urine-grown algae would be restricted to non-food/biostimulant markets (scale caveat).

hydrophobic gas-permeable membrane ammonia stripping into H2SO4
Free NH3 diffuses through PTFE membrane into acid, forming ammonium sulfate without air stripping energy.
Yield = 8 g N/L × 4.7 kg AS/kg N × 80%. Could feed a green-ammonia/fuel-cell demo instead.
evaporative crystallisation of chloride salts; dioxin-bearing solids to thermal treatment
Chloride flux salts are highly soluble and recrystallise for reuse in rotary furnaces.
Chloride share estimate ~35% × 85%. Salt-slag processors (e.g. Befesa) do this commercially. Price estimate ~half virgin flux salt cost.
HCl leach of Al2O3/AlN residue → basification to polyaluminium chloride
Reactive alumina dissolves in HCl; controlled partial neutralisation polymerises Al13 Keggin species, the active coagulant.
Yield estimate: residue Al2O3 ~30% of dust, PAC at ~30% Al2O3 basis. Cost estimate dominated by HCl. Must verify dioxin/F removal for water-treatment use.
Layered double hydroxide sorbent (from brine Mg + Al waste)
Layered double hydroxide sorbent (from brine Mg + Al waste)
co-precipitation with Mg2+ from SWRO brine at pH 10 → Mg-Al LDH
Waste aluminate and brine Mg form hydrotalcite; its exchangeable interlayer captures phosphate/fluoride/PFAS.
Yield estimate: ~0.15 kg Al/kg dust × ~11 kg LDH/kg Al × ~60% (Mg from ~150 kg brine per kg dust). LDH $10/kg is speciality sorbent value; niche market (scale caveat).
Fluoride and alumina act as mineralisers that lower clinkering temperature and fuel use.
Price estimate (fluorspar-mineraliser displacement, discounted). Chloride limit in cement kilns is the constraint.
chemical demineralisation (1 M HCl) + deproteinisation (1 M NaOH) → chitin; deacetylation 50% NaOH 100 °C → chitosan
HCl dissolves CaCO3, NaOH hydrolyses protein; concentrated hot alkali removes acetyl groups converting chitin to chitosan.
Yield = 25% DM × ~25% chitin (15-40% range) × 0.8 chitin→chitosan. Cost estimate ~$10-12/kg chitosan production cost × 0.05. Commercial (China, India, Norway).
electrospinning chitosan/PEO into nanofibre hemostatic or antibacterial film
Protonated chitosan amines bind erythrocytes/platelets and bacterial membranes; nanofibre mats give high surface area for hemostasis.

Calibration-example route. Price uses medical-grade chitosan ($217) as bulk-equivalent rather than the research-scale dressing price ($1000, research_quantity). Yield after purification losses ~60%. Cost estimate.
lactic-acid fermentation 5-7 d (biological demineralisation/deproteinisation), mild NaOH finish, deacetylation
LAB ferment whey lactose to lactic acid in situ, dissolving CaCO3 as calcium lactate and activating shrimp proteases; this replaces most HCl/NaOH.
Tnuva: outlet for surplus whey/permeate lactose
Yield slightly below chemical route (incomplete deproteinisation). Cost estimate reduced vs chemical route. Whey-driven LAB fermentation of shrimp waste is published at lab scale.
partial deacetylation/TEMPO oxidation + high-pressure homogenisation to chitin nanofibrils
Surface charge introduced on chitin microfibrils allows mechanical fibrillation into ~10-20 nm nanofibers for Pickering emulsions, films and wound care.
Yield = chitin 0.0625 × 80%. Price $100 speciality; market small (Marine Akwa, Mahtani). Cost estimate incl. homogenisation energy.
green extraction with natural deep eutectic solvent or vegetable oil, then concentration
Astaxanthin (esterified, bound to crustacyanin) partitions into lipophilic solvents once proteins are denatured.
Yield = ~100 mg/kg DM astaxanthin × 25% DM × 60% recovery. Price $700 is for shrimp-waste astaxanthin (feed grade). Pairs with chitin route as a front-end step.
hot-water/ethanol extraction, adsorption-resin purification, spray-dry to OPC extract
Oligomeric procyanidins are water/ethanol soluble and are enriched on polymeric resins.

Yield estimate: ~1% OPC extract on dry bark × 60% DM. Price proxy = grade seed OPC ($30); branded Pycnogenol (Horphag) sells far higher. Commercial (novelty 2). Israel has little pine bark (planted forests small).
hot-water/sulfite extraction of condensed tannins, spray dry
Condensed tannins (flavan-3-ol polymers) are extracted and used as phenol substitutes in wood adhesives.
Yield estimate: 15% tannin on dry bark (10-20% range) × 60% DM. Pine-tannin adhesives commercial in NZ/Chile.
acid-catalysed self-blowing polycondensation of tannin + furfuryl alcohol (+ diethyl ether blowing)
Flavonoid A-rings react with furfuryl alcohol carbocations; exotherm vaporises blowing agent giving a rigid, inherently flame-retardant phenolic-like foam.

Yield = tannin 0.09 → foam ~1.7× tannin mass (furfuryl alcohol added; its cost in process cost). Price estimate set below phenolic foam (~$4-6/kg). Pizzi/Celzard group papers; no commercial plant known.

Zeolite NaP1/X from coal fly ash (sorbent)
two-step alkaline hydrothermal zeolitisation (2 M NaOH, 80-150 °C, 24-48 h)
NaOH dissolves the Si/Al glass phase; Na-aluminosilicate gel recrystallises as Na-P1 zeolite with high NH4+/heavy-metal cation-exchange capacity.

Yield 0.57 kg Na-P1/kg ash at ~65% purity (range 0.25 high-purity to 0.98 crude). Cost estimate: ~0.6 kg NaOH/kg ash (Wdowin pilot: 12 kg NaOH per 20 kg ash) partly recycled → ~$0.25 + energy. 10 m3 pilot reactors reported. Product use: NH4+ removal from dairy/sludge centrate in Israel.

Zeolite for CO2 capture (13X) from waste
Zeolite for CO2 capture (13X) from waste
Fusion converts quartz/mullite to soluble Na-silicates/aluminates; adjusting Si/Al gives faujasite (13X) with high CO2 affinity.

Yield estimate by analogy with fusion Na-A route (ACS IECR 2017, 7.1-yr payback for Na-A). 13X CO2 grade requires purity; price $5/kg is catalogue. Cost estimate: NaOH ~1.2 kg/kg ash partly recycled + fusion energy.

Mixed rare-earth concentrate from coal fly ash/acid mine drainage
acid leach (HCl/HNO3) → solvent extraction to mixed REO concentrate
REE in coal ash sit in the glass phase and phosphate grains; alkali roast opens the glass so mineral acid can leach REE, then D2EHPA SX concentrates them.

Yield estimate: ~300 ppm REO in typical coal ash x ~70% recovery; Israeli ash from imported S-African/Colombian/Russian coal, REE content unmeasured. Value per kg ash is tiny unless coupled with zeolite/SCM co-products. US DOE pilots exist.

Cenospheres are gas-filled glass bubbles (density <1) formed in the boiler; they float off in water and serve as lightweight fillers for syntactic foams, oil-well cements, and polymer composites.

Price estimate $0.5-1.5/kg bulk cenospheres (midpoint used, no single sourced quote). Yield 0.01-1% of ash (0.3% assumed; Israeli ash content unknown). Commercial elsewhere → novelty 2. Demo: float test in a beaker.
coal fly ash (pulverised coal plants; Israel: Orot Rabin & Rutenberg)
alkali-activated geopolymer mortar for 3D printing (fly ash + waste-glass activator + sand)
Waste glass fines dissolved in NaOH give a sodium silicate activator replacing commercial water glass; it polycondenses fly-ash aluminosilicate into N-A-S-H gel.

Yield = kg printable mortar per kg ash (binder ~40% of mortar incl. sand). Price is catalogue $0.5/kg mortar. Cost estimate: NaOH + sand + admixtures ~$0.08/kg mortar. Symbiosis with unrecyclable glass cullet fines (MATMIN-0084). co2 vs OPC mortar, estimate.
Tomato pomace (skins and seeds) from paste processing
Suberin/cutin-based polyester (from tomato peel, cork waste)
Suberin/cutin-based polyester (from tomato peel, cork waste)
aqueous alkaline hydrolysis 120-130 °C → acid precipitation of cutin monomers (10,16-diHHDA) → bio-lacquer/polyester resin
Cutin is a polyester of C16/C18 hydroxy fatty acids; saponification releases 10,16-dihydroxyhexadecanoic acid, which is re-polymerised into crosslinked polyester can linings.

Yield: 25% DM x ~55% skins in dry pomace x 12% cutin (pilot 10-15%; lab up to 32-46% with HPH). Cost estimate (NaOH, heat, drying). TomaPaint pilot 100 kg/h → novelty 3. Israel tomato-paste volume small.
Tomato pomace (skins and seeds) from paste processing
solvent or supercritical CO2 extraction → lycopene oleoresin
Lycopene is concentrated in tomato skin chromoplasts; non-polar extraction recovers it as an oleoresin.

Yield estimate: ~0.1% lycopene of pomace DM x 0.25 DM x 70% recovery. Price $296/kg catalogue is for pure lycopene; oleoresin sells lower. Israel fit 4: Lycored (Beer Sheva) is a world lycopene leader → local buyer.
Tomato pomace (skins and seeds) from paste processing
cold pressing / hexane extraction of tomato seeds
Tomato seeds hold ~20-25% oil rich in linoleic acid, extractable mechanically.
Yield estimate: 0.25 DM x 45% seeds x 22% oil x 85% recovery. Niche cosmetic oil.
Tomato pomace (skins and seeds) from paste processing
PFAS-free grease/water barrier coating for paper food-service (cutin hydroxy-acid polyester)
PFAS-free grease/water barrier coating for paper food-service (cutin hydroxy-acid polyester)
cutin monomer → melt polycondensation → aqueous dispersion coated on paperboard
Hydroxy-fatty-acid polyesters are intrinsically hydrophobic/oleophobic enough to replace fluorinated grease barriers on paper.
Price estimate: bio-based barrier coatings ~$10-20/kg (midpoint), no direct quote. EU/US PFAS bans in food packaging create pull. Pairs with pizza-box/food-service paper streams.
Tomato pomace (skins and seeds) from paste processing
lycopene extraction with excess d-limonene (orange terpenes) as bio-solvent, then vacuum strip limonene for reuse
Lycopene is highly soluble in limonene (similar non-polar terpene); waste citrus terpenes replace hexane, giving a food-grade oleoresin.
Yield as lycopene route. Symbiosis with excess orange-terpene stream (CHEMBIO-0243); Israel has citrus processing plus Lycored. Demo: shake-extract, colour reading.
saponification (NaOH, aq. MeOH 85 °C) → solvent extraction → crystallisation of β-sitosterol
About 15% of pitch is free+esterified sterols; saponification frees them and they crystallise selectively.

Yield 9.8% sterol of pitch at 93% purity (CNKI); patent: TOP 14-15% sterols, >70% recovery. Commercial (sterol producers use TOP). Cost estimate (solvent losses, energy). No Israeli kraft pulp → israel_fit 1.
Mycolicibacterium whole-cell side-chain cleavage of phytosterols to AD/ADD
Engineered mycobacteria degrade the sterol C17 side-chain while keeping the steroid nucleus, giving androstenedione, the key precursor of corticoid and sex hormones.

Yield estimate: 0.098 sterol x ~0.69 mass ratio (MW 286/414) x ~90% conversion. Price estimate $30-50/kg (midpoint) for bulk AD, unsourced. Commercial from soy sterols; using pitch sterols directly is less common. Israel pharma (Teva) is a buyer.
C22-C24 fatty alcohols (behenyl/lignoceryl) from pitch wax esters
C22-C24 fatty alcohols (behenyl/lignoceryl) from pitch wax esters
mother-liquor fractionation by vacuum distillation / crystallisation
TOP contains ~10% bound C22-C26 wax alcohols that co-extract with sterols and remain in the mother liquor; distillation gives behenyl/lignoceryl-rich cuts for cosmetics emollients.
Composition from patent (~10% wax alcohols); recovery 40% assumed. Price estimate: behenyl alcohol ~$4-6/kg, unsourced.
co-hydrotreating with crude tall oil in renewable diesel units
Fatty/rosin acid fraction is deoxygenated to paraffins; heavy sterol/polymer fraction needs pre-separation.
Textbook-ish baseline (energy). Yield estimate: ~40% hydrotreatable acids/neutrals. Current fate is burning as mill fuel.
esterification of pitch fatty/rosin acids with glycerol-foots glycerol → polyol-ester lubricant / tackifier
Glycerol from refining residue esterifies the C18 fatty and rosin acids into tri-esters (ester gum / biolubricant); two low-value residues combine into one ester product.
Yield estimate: ~40% acids in pitch x ~75% to ester. Product quality (colour, odour) unknown; refs only for ester-gum chemistry.
WWTP coarse screenings (rags, wipes, plastics from bar screens)
hygienising + drying + fluffing/pelletising of cellulose/viscose fibre fraction
Toilet-paper and viscose wipe fibres are intact cellulose; once washed and sanitised they work as stabilising fibres in stone-mastic asphalt or as insulation.

Yield estimate: 20% DS x ~40% cellulose of DS x 70% recovery. Commercial Cellvation/Recell is on fine sieves (<0.35 mm); coarse bar screenings are dirtier. Price estimate: asphalt cellulose fibre ~$0.3-0.6/kg, unsourced. Avoids $55/t disposal.
WWTP coarse screenings (rags, wipes, plastics from bar screens)
enzymatic/mechanical fibrillation of recovered cellulose to CNF
Recovered fibre keeps the cellulose I backbone, so it can be fibrillated to nanofibrils like virgin pulp.
Australian WWTP study (2026) made CNF from recovered screenings cellulose. Yield estimate ~half of recovered cellulose after bleaching. Hygiene perception limits markets → use in construction/paper.
WWTP coarse screenings (rags, wipes, plastics from bar screens)
pyrolysis 700-800 °C + steam activation of mixed screenings to sorbent char
Carbonising cellulose/plastics mix yields a mesoporous carbon; high-T activation gives sites that adsorb PFAS from the same WWTP effluent (closed-loop).
Yield estimate: 20% DS x 20% char yield. No paper on screenings-derived PFAS sorbents found; analogous sludge-biochar PFAS work exists. Pyrolysis also destroys pathogens.
WWTP coarse screenings (rags, wipes, plastics from bar screens)
Aromatic polyester polyol from PET wipe fibres (glycerolysis)
glycerolysis of PET fibres with glycerol-foots glycerol (Zn acetate, 200-220 °C)
Glycerol transesterifies PET into hydroxyl-terminated terephthalate oligoesters usable as polyols in rigid PU/PIR foam.
Yield estimate: PET ~20% of screenings DS (0.04 kg/kg) + glycerol mass. Price estimate: aromatic polyester polyols ~$1.8-2.5/kg. Contamination tolerance of PU polyols unknown.

Mixed rare-earth concentrate from coal fly ash/acid mine drainage
HCl leach → oxalate precipitation to mixed REO concentrate
REE sit in apatite and clay-adsorbed phases; calcination breaks clay structure so acid leaching recovers ~73-81% of REE.

Yield: ~300 ppm REE in dry clay (122-515) x 40% solids x 73% recovery. Price $20 = catalogue mixed concentrate (basis per kg REO assumed). Cost estimate (calcination + acid per kg wet slurry). Israeli Negev phosphate slimes REE grade unmeasured.
phosphate rock beneficiation tailings and clay slimes (global)
Phosphate rock concentrate (~30% P2O5) recovered from slimes
Phosphate rock concentrate (~30% P2O5) recovered from slimes
Fine apatite grains lost to the slimes can be floated after desliming; 94% P2O5 recovery reported.
Yield: 40% solids x 7% P2O5 x 94% recovery / 30% grade. Price estimate: phosphate rock ~$150/t (2024 range $120-200). Israel fit 4: ICL Rotem/Oron slimes, local buyer.
phosphate rock beneficiation tailings and clay slimes (global)
size classification and drying of the fibrous clay fraction
Phosphate slimes are rich in needle-like palygorskite whose high surface area gives gel/rheology and sorbent properties (drilling muds, agrochemical carriers).
Yield estimate: ~25% of dry solids attapulgite recoverable. Price estimate: industrial attapulgite $200-400/t. Purity vs commercial deposits unknown.
phosphate rock beneficiation tailings and clay slimes (global)
flash calcination 750-800 °C → blend as calcined clay in LC3 cement
Calcining the smectite/kaolinite-bearing clay dehydroxylates it to a reactive pozzolan, replacing clinker.
Yield: 40% solids less ~12% LOI. Pozzolanic reactivity of smectite-rich slimes is lower than kaolinite, so it is uncertain. Drying cost dominates (60% water).
phosphate rock beneficiation tailings and clay slimes (global)
Mixed rare-earth concentrate from coal fly ash/acid mine drainage
Mixed rare-earth concentrate from coal fly ash/acid mine drainage
leach REE and P from slimes with TiO2-industry spent weak sulfuric acid instead of fresh acid
Waste 20-25% H2SO4 dissolves apatite and releases REE (and acid is consumed rather than neutralised), coupling two acid/alkaline-earth wastes.
Yield: 300 ppm x 0.4 x 61% (sulfuric/phosphoric leach recovery on flotation tailings, Minerals 2018). Fe/Ti impurities from the weak acid complicate SX.
Sheep/goat crutchings, dags and low-grade wool at farm
aqueous detergent scouring → centrifuge wool grease → refine to lanolin
Wool grease (wax esters of sterols/fatty alcohols) emulsifies in hot scour liquor and is centrifuged off.
Moisture blank in DB; yield estimate: ~8% grease of greasy dirty wool x 50% refined lanolin. Commercial scouring practice; low-grade dags usually not scoured.
Sheep/goat crutchings, dags and low-grade wool at farm
pelletise wool for slow-release N fertiliser / water retention
Keratin (~16% N) mineralises slowly in soil, and wool fibre retains water.
Commercial wool pellets exist (novelty 2). Yield estimate (dirt loss). Textbook baseline.
Sheep/goat crutchings, dags and low-grade wool at farm
HCl hydrolysis → cystine crystallisation → electrochemical reduction to L-cysteine
Wool keratin is ~11-13% cystine; acid hydrolysis frees it and its low solubility allows crystallisation.
Yield estimate: 60% clean wool x 11% cystine x 50% recovery. Commercial from feathers/hair in China.
Sheep/goat crutchings, dags and low-grade wool at farm
sulfitolysis or reductive (L-cysteine/urea) keratin extraction → dialysis → freeze-dried sponge / electrospun mat
Breaking disulfide bonds solubilises keratin; regenerated keratin has cell-adhesion motifs (LDV/RGD) for wound-healing scaffolds.
Yield estimate: 60% clean wool x ~25% extractable to biomedical-grade. $200/kg is specialty; dirty dags need extensive cleaning.
Sheep/goat crutchings, dags and low-grade wool at farm
carbonisation 600 °C → KOH activation 800 °C → N,S-co-doped porous carbon
Keratin carries N and S that remain as heteroatom dopants, raising pseudocapacitance and Li-S polysulfide binding.
Yield estimate: ~20% char x ~50% after activation, x clean fraction. Papers on hair/wool-derived doped carbons exist; no specific ref verified.
Sheep/goat crutchings, dags and low-grade wool at farm
alkaline hydrolysis of wool using spent dairy CIP caustic (NaOH ~1-2%) at 90 °C → neutralise → keratin peptide biostimulant
Spent CIP caustic still carries free NaOH; it hydrolyses keratin into soluble peptides/amino acids for foliar biostimulants, consuming alkali that would otherwise need neutralising.
Yield estimate (solubilised protein + salts). Residual milk organics in CIP liquor are compatible. Na load in product must be checked for soil salinity in Israel.
Spent mammalian cell culture media (biopharma harvest)
Recycled defined microbial fermentation feed (spent CHO media)
Recycled defined microbial fermentation feed (spent CHO media)
use as feed (plus 2% glycerol) for E. coli recombinant-protein fermentation
Chemically defined media leave unused amino acids, vitamins and trace metals after CHO culture, which support E. coli growth at ~94% of LB and similar protein titres.
Price estimate: value as replacement of ready-to-use microbial medium ~$0.03-0.1 per litre (midpoint), unsourced. Israel: Teva, Kamada, Pluri biopharma; Carasso fermentation facility could reuse it.
Spent mammalian cell culture media (biopharma harvest)
feed to Trametes versicolor fermentation producing beta/alpha glucans
CHO spent media replaced corn-steep liquor and doubled glucan yield in T. versicolor culture.
Yield estimate ~2 g glucan/L. Price uses yeast beta-glucan catalogue ($40) as proxy for fungal glucans.
Spent mammalian cell culture media (biopharma harvest)
mixotrophic microalgae (Chlorella) cultivation on spent media
Residual glucose, lactate, amino acids and ammonium serve as C and N for mixotrophic Chlorella growth.
Yield estimate ~2 g/L dry biomass. Food-grade claims are unlikely from pharma waste, so value is for non-food algae.
Spent mammalian cell culture media (biopharma harvest)
PHB fermentation (Cupriavidus/engineered E. coli) on spent media plus crude-glycerol carbon
Spent media supply N, P and trace nutrients and crude glycerol supplies the carbon excess needed for PHA accumulation under nutrient limitation.
Yield estimate: 20 g/L glycerol x 0.3 g PHB/g. Ref supports media-reuse + glycerol only, not PHB specifically.
open-air market (shuk) produce waste (e.g. Carmel, Mahane Yehuda)
Easily degradable sugars/starches convert to CH4.
Textbook baseline. Yield estimate: 13% VS x 0.4 m3 CH4/kg VS x 0.717 kg/m3. co2 estimate vs landfill.

black soldier fly larvae bioconversion → dry/defat to meal
BSF larvae convert fruit/veg sugars and protein into larval biomass (~40% protein DM).
Yield estimate: ~15-20% wet larvae on wet substrate → ~0.05 dry meal. Commercial elsewhere. Shuk waste is sorted and clean, which helps.
open-air market (shuk) produce waste (e.g. Carmel, Mahane Yehuda)
Fruit/veg sugars (~8% fresh) are converted homofermentatively to lactic acid at 0.6-0.9 g/g.
Yield estimate: 8% sugars x 0.65. Downstream purification is costly for mixed waste.
open-air market (shuk) produce waste (e.g. Carmel, Mahane Yehuda)
co-fermentation of produce juice + cheese whey (lactose, N, minerals) to L-lactic acid
Whey supplies lactose and nitrogen (replacing yeast extract), while produce juice supplies glucose/fructose and buffering minerals.
Yield estimate on combined sugars. Fits Israeli dairy-whey + urban organics. Refs on whey/fruit co-fermentation exist but none verified.
open-air market (shuk) produce waste (e.g. Carmel, Mahane Yehuda)
aqueous-ethanol extraction → immobilise in starch/chitosan film
Anthocyanins change colour with pH, so films detect amines and CO2 from spoiling fish/meat.
Yield estimate: ~0.05% anthocyanin of total market waste (only a small fraction is purple produce). Price estimate for indicator-grade extract. Value is the demo, not the volume.
SiC abrasive debris oxidises at firing temperature, releasing CO/CO2 inside the viscous glassy phase and foaming the body into a lightweight insulating ceramic.
Yield: 60% solids less ~8% LOI. Price is catalogue glass-ceramic tile. Israel has small tile production (Negev Ceramics). No Israeli tonnage.
Fines are compatible with ceramic body chemistry at low dosage.
Baseline/current fate (body recycling). Limited by foaming at high dosage.
hydrocyclone/dense-media separation of SiC grains from glassy fines
SiC (density 3.2, very hard) separates from the silicate glass (2.4) by gravity, so it can be reused as abrasive.
Yield estimate: SiC ~3% of dry sludge, 50% recovery. Price estimate: black SiC grit $1-2/kg. Grain size may be too fine to reuse.
alkali activation (NaOH/silicate) of glassy polishing fines + MgO
The amorphous porcelain glass fines dissolve in alkali and form N-A-S-H gel, and residual MgO adds M-S-H.
Yield estimate. Strength data on this specific sludge not verified.
sinter-foam 850-950 °C using sludge SiC as the foaming agent
SiC in the sludge replaces purchased SiC/carbon foaming agents; unrecyclable glass fines provide the low-melting matrix for foam-glass aggregate.
Yield per kg sludge (dry share). Symbiosis with glass cullet fines (MATMIN-0084).
hot dilute-acid (HNO3/citric, pH 1.5, 80 °C) extraction → ethanol precipitation
Beet pectin (~25% DM) is highly acetylated with feruloyl side chains; acid extraction solubilises it, and it gels poorly but is an excellent emulsifier.

Yield: 22% DM x 25% pectin x 50% recovery. Beet pectin sells below citrus pectin (emulsifier niche, commercial) so the $14 catalogue price is an upper bound. Israel has no beet sugar industry (Kiryat Gat plant closed).
high-shear homogenisation of parenchyma cellulose into MFC / platelets (Curran-type)
Beet parenchyma cell walls (thin primary walls, low lignin) fibrillate easily into cellulose platelets for paints, drilling muds and composites.
Yield estimate: 22% DM x ~25% cellulose recoverable. Commercial (CelluComp Curran).
alkaline or feruloyl-esterase hydrolysis → adsorption resin purification of ferulic acid
Ferulic acid is ester-linked to arabinan/galactan side chains (~0.8% DM); esterases or mild alkali release it.
Yield estimate: 0.22 x 0.8% x 60%. Can feed vanillin bioconversion.
mild acid hydrolysis of arabinan → chromatographic separation → crystallisation
Beet pulp arabinan (~20% DM) is the richest arabinose source; it hydrolyses more easily than other glycosidic bonds, so it can be released selectively.
Yield estimate: 0.22 x 18% x 50%. Price estimate: L-arabinose food grade $10-20/kg (China), unsourced.
Laccase-crosslinked ferulated beet-pectin hydrogel (bioink / wound dressing)
Laccase-crosslinked ferulated beet-pectin hydrogel (bioink / wound dressing)
enzymatic oxidative gelation (laccase/peroxidase) forming diferulate crosslinks
Feruloyl groups on beet pectin dimerise under laccase into covalent diferulic bridges, forming a cell-friendly hydrogel without calcium.
Price estimate for research hydrogel material ($50-200/kg), small market. Demo: gel forms in minutes with commercial laccase.
beet-pulp MFC as viscosity-modifying/anti-shrinkage admixture in 3D-printed fly-ash geopolymer
At 0.1-0.5% dosage, cellulose microfibrils give thixotropy (shape retention) and bridge microcracks in printable alkali-activated mortars.
Value counted as MFC price. Symbiosis with coal fly ash (MATMIN-0001). Dosage-limited market.
Post-consumer MDF offcuts and furniture panel trim
Recovered MDF wood fibre (for new MDF/wood-fibre insulation)
Recovered MDF wood fibre (for new MDF/wood-fibre insulation)
steam or ohmic heating hydrolysis of UF bonds → refining to fibre
Cured UF resin hydrolyses in hot water/steam, freeing the fibres for reuse.
Price estimate: recovered fibre valued near pulpwood fibre ($0.15-0.25/kg). MDF Recovery Ltd (UK) commercialising → novelty 2. Israel imports most panels; furniture trim exists.
Post-consumer MDF offcuts and furniture panel trim
Clean wood-based panel waste can partly replace virgin chips.
Textbook baseline. Process cost estimate includes resin and pressing.
Post-consumer MDF offcuts and furniture panel trim
pyrolysis 600 °C → KOH activation 800 °C → N-doped porous carbon
UF resin (~8-10% of MDF) carries ~3% N into the char as pyridinic/pyrrolic dopants, boosting capacitance and CO2 uptake.
Yield estimate: ~25% char x ~50% after activation. Papers exist on N-doped carbons from MDF but none verified here. Formaldehyde off-gas must be handled.
Post-consumer MDF offcuts and furniture panel trim
mycelium (Ganoderma/Pleurotus) grown through recovered fibre → moulded packaging
Fungal hyphae bind the fibres into a light foam-like composite; steaming lowers formaldehyde that would inhibit growth.
Price is catalogue mycelium packaging ($3.5/kg). Formaldehyde tolerance of fungi is unverified. Process cost estimate.
Post-consumer MDF offcuts and furniture panel trim
twin-screw compounding with recycled PP strapping (50:50) → WPC profiles
Wood fibre reinforces the PP matrix (with MAPP coupling agent); both are low-value logistics/furniture residues.
Yield as product mass attributable to the MDF fibre half (1 kg fibre → 2 kg compound, credited 1). Symbiosis with PP strapping (URBANX-0233).
PS unzips by beta-scission into its monomer at high selectivity, unlike PE/PP.
Yield ~60% styrene (stream notes; up to 70%+). Commercial pilots/plants (Agilyx, Pyrowave). Cost and co2 are estimates.
selective dissolution (CreaSolv-type) → filtration → precipitation, HBCDD separated and destroyed
PS dissolves in specific solvents while additives and HBCDD stay in the liquor, giving virgin-like PS.
Price estimate vs virgin PS ~$1.3-1.6/kg. PolyStyreneLoop (NL) demo plant → novelty 2.
Friedel-Crafts knitting (FeCl3 + formaldehyde dimethyl acetal) → wash → dry
External crosslinkers knit aromatic rings into a rigid microporous network (BET 500-1000 m2/g) that adsorbs organics and CO2.
Price estimate: polymeric adsorbent resins $10-50/kg (low end). Uses chlorinated solvent; greener knitting under study.
sulfonation with conc. H2SO4 (or acetyl sulfate) 60-80 °C → neutralise
Electrophilic aromatic sulfonation adds SO3H groups to the phenyl rings, giving cation-exchange or water-soluble polyelectrolyte.
Price estimate (ion-exchange resin $2-5/kg bulk). Mass gain from SO3H.
dissolve EPS in surplus d-limonene (orange terpenes) at collection point → distil limonene → PS
Limonene dissolves EPS (shrinking volume ~20x) and can be distilled off, so EPS logistics and citrus-terpene surplus solve each other.
Sony demonstrated limonene EPS recycling in the 1990s (not widespread). Price estimate as above. Partner CHEMBIO-0243 (excess orange terpenes).

indirect carbonation: NH4Cl leach of Ca → bubble CO2 → precipitated CaCO3

Yield estimate: ~8% leachable CaO in fines x 1.78 CaCO3/CaO. Catalogue PCC price is low ($0.11). co2 = CO2 bound.

accelerated carbonation of RCA in a reactor fed with brewery fermentation CO2
Hydrated cement phases react with CO2 to form CaCO3, densifying the RCA (lower water absorption) and storing CO2 permanently.
Yield includes ~4% CO2 uptake (estimate). FastCarb (France) piloted RCA carbonation with cement-kiln CO2. Pure fermentation CO2 avoids capture cost.

Ca(OH)2/CaCO3 in the fines neutralise H2SO4, forming gypsum and leaving amorphous silica, replacing purchased lime.

Fruit kernel oils (apricot, peach, cherry, mango)
expeller/hexane extraction → fractionation of mango kernel fat (stearin = CBE, cosmetic mango butter)

aqueous-acetone extraction of gallotannins → tannase hydrolysis → gallic acid crystallisation

Iron-gall chemistry: Fe3+ chelates the galloyl catechols, forming insoluble blue-black complexes (used as ink, textile mordant black, wood stain).
Price estimate for natural black colourant ($5-15/kg). Zn in galvanising liquor must be removed first. Benchtop demo in minutes.
thermoplastic starch film with in-situ tannin antioxidant/UV barrier
Native kernel tannins crosslink and protect starch films, giving active antioxidant packaging.
Yield estimate (starch + glycerol). Value at catalogue TPS price.

Powdered activated carbon (municipal water / food decolorisation)
Steam gasifies part of the carbon, opening micropores (40-50% burn-off).

Graphene nanoplatelets (from biochar or flash Joule heating)
flash Joule heating (3000 K, ms) → turbostratic graphene
High-current discharge resistively heats the conductive char to ~3000 K, rearranging sp2 carbon into turbostratic graphene (Tour group).

compound annealed char into polymer/cement for EMI shielding
